text:
Writers, stop writing "She realized."

Not this: She realized he had never loved her.
Try this: She scrolled his contacts. Three years, and he still had her saved as "Priya (work)."

Don't announce the realization. Hand over the evidence.

#writingcommunity

Rewrite in one line, without the word "realized":

"She realized the message wasn't from him."

Reply with yours. I'll quote-post my favourite tomorrow.

Writers: how to write jealousy without the word "jealous."

Not this: She felt jealous when she saw Mira's promotion post.
Try this: She liked Mira's post, unliked it, then liked it again.

Jealousy is attention you never meant to pay.

#writingcommunity

Writers, stop writing "felt."

Not this: She felt a rush of relief.
Try this: Her shoulders dropped an inch.

"Felt" reports. A body shows.

#writingcommunity

Which line puts you in the scene?
- She felt nervous.
- She checked the clock.

#writingcommunity #amwriting

Writers, stop writing "Suddenly."

Not this: Suddenly, the phone rang.
Try this: She had one hand on the tap when the phone rang.

Surprise lives in placement. Put the event last.

#writingcommunity #amwriting #writingtips

Most reading apps show you what you already like.

I'm building WritOn to hold back about a fifth of your feed for stories you'd never have picked.

Comfortable reading is easy. Growing taste needs a little friction.

#writingcommunity #indieauthors

Stop describing your character in a mirror.

Not this: She looked in the mirror. Brown eyes, long hair, a small scar on her chin.
Try this: She pressed a thumb over the scar on her chin, the way she had since the fall.

Describe with a gesture, not a checklist.

#writingcommunity

Generation Scaled. CI Didn't.

AI can generate the feature in minutes.
Then:
CI runs.
Tests multiply.
Staging queues.
Another agent opens another PR.

The software bottleneck didn't disappear.
It moved downstream.
Generation scaled. CI didn't.

#AI #DevOps #SoftwareEngineering

tweets.text:
Why AI Coding Is Turning CI Into the New Bottleneck

1/
AI solved one software-development bottleneck and immediately exposed another.

Code generation got dramatically faster.
CI/CD didn't.

2/
Coding agents can generate:
features
tests
refactors
pull requests
in minutes.

Every one of those changes still has to be validated.

3/
So higher code velocity creates:
more builds
more test runs
more staging environments
more queues
more infrastructure pressure

4/
The strange result:

AI may finish writing before the engineering system is ready to evaluate what it wrote.

5/
Current engineering discussions are already reporting long CI turnaround times as synthetic code volume increases.

https://drive.google.com/file/d/1k24QYbSVsp1tywMAICA2zL_wKAH9pHoT/view

6/
That may force a rethink of the entire workflow:
• What actually needs remote CI?
• What can run locally?
• What can be checked deterministically before entering the pipeline?

7/
The AI coding race has mostly measured generation speed.

The next important metric may be:
time-to-confidence.

8/
Generation scaled.
Verification and infrastructure didn't.

That's the new choke point.

#AI #DevOps #SoftwareEngineering

text:
Writers: how to write silence without "there was a pause."

Not this: There was an awkward silence after he asked.
Try this: The fridge hummed. A tap dripped. Neither of them reached for the tea.

Silence is never empty. Name what fills it.

#writingcommunity #amwriting

New writers, stop hunting for synonyms for "said."

Not this: "I'm fine," she exclaimed defensively.
Try this: "I'm fine." She wiped the clean counter again.

"Said" disappears. A beat of action stays.

#writingcommunity #newwriter #writingadvice

The Cognitive Fast

AI writes code faster. But it can quietly weaken what matters most: understanding the system in your head.

Some developers are stepping back to rebuild deep comprehension.

Speed is useful.
Mental models are durable.

#AI #SoftwareEngineering #Coding

The FOSS Defiance

Open source maintainers never asked for infinite pull requests.

AI generates contributions faster than humans can review or maintain them.

More PRs ≠ healthier software.

The real debate: protecting attention, not increasing output.

#OpenSource #AI #FOSS

Round-up: quote-post the best 1-2 replies of the week, one line each on why they work.
If there are none: Fix this line without a single adverb: "I'm fine," she exclaimed defensively.

#writingcommunity #amwriting #writerslife

Writers, stop writing "As you know" dialogue.

Not this: "As you know, Dad, since Mom died three years ago, we've run the shop alone."
Try this: "You still hang her apron there." "It's where it goes."

Characters never explain what both already know.

#writingcommunity

tweets.text:
A writer can rank in search and still never gain a reader.

The trend data around AI search for fiction authors highlights a critical shift: once someone discovers your story, what gives them a reason to return? (1/3)

A search result can introduce the work. But discovery only buys a first impression.

A memorable character, a consistent publishing rhythm, and a place to continue the conversation can build the relationship. (2/3)

For fiction writers, the practical test is simple: after someone finishes one piece, is their next step clear?

What has brought readers back to your writing?

#fictionwriting #indieauthors #writingcommunity #storytelling #writon (3/3)

text:
Writers: how to write exhaustion without "tired."

Not this: She was so tired she couldn't think straight.
Try this: She read the same email three times and still couldn't say who sent it.

Exhaustion shrinks the world to one unfinished task.

#writingcommunity #amwriting

Exhaustion is a behavior, not a word. What do you actually do when you're too tired to think?
- Reread the same line
- Stare at the fridge
- Scroll without reading
- Make tea, forget it

#writingcommunity #writerslife #authorlife #amwriting

Writers: how to write loneliness without "alone."

Not this: He felt alone in the big, empty flat.
Try this: He took two cups down, then put one back.

Loneliness is a habit built for two.

#writingcommunity #writingtips #amwriting #flashfiction
